BiblicalUsage: Aftergrowth is the crop nobody planted, the grain that springs up of itself in the second year. God gave it to Hezekiah as a sign, that Judah would eat what grew of itself, then sow and reap in the third year.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God feeds His people from ground they never worked, and the aftergrowth is His promise that provision does not depend on our planting.
